column8: Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2) store: Census 7115 fills the inside years Q1c-003 left unread, 2009 the one down year (-6.2%), back above 2008 in 2011; checks against the data file; say artists, writers and performers (row 37).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2): sizes l.9's smaller as 6-10% of an occupation's receipts in 2009 (0.17 and 0.27 check), but never beside shares' 36.55% as if her career were a sixth as risky: l.9's smaller means smaller than good years, and an aggregate is far smoother than one career (advances cut to a quarter, Q1-030).
Wed 18 Nov: store only: the slump's depth and length in one figure ($1.16bn, about 8% of a year; checks); no part needs it.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 21, which carries the 2009 shape (businesses -0.8%, each -5.4%; checks) beside 2020's.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2): the closest official cut to a writer paid as a person, sole proprietors -7.8% in 2009 and back above 2008 in 2011 (checks); if a figure is ever quoted, this or NAICS 711's -10.0% beats the arts sector's -11.6% in SKELETON 2.3's evidence line, which includes gyms and amusement parks.

Wed 18 Nov: store: beside other one-person businesses the artists' 2009 fall was ordinary (-6.2% against -4.1%; per business -5.4% against -5.7%; checks); a guard against saying the arts fell far more than the economy.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 6 (share of all nonemployer receipts 1.51%, 1.48%, 1.50%; checks); travels as its one clause.

Wed 18 Nov: CANON B4 for side: on tax and census records the occupation fell 3 to 5 times nominal GDP in 2009 (checks); never cite the national accounts for it (Q1c-008); the IRS line is NAICS 711, with performing-arts companies and sports.
Wed 18 Nov: same IRS series as Q1c-005: the NAICS 711 2008 line (receipts +2.8% while shares fell 36.55%) travels with it as one clause, as Q1c-007 does.
Wed 18 Nov: the tax recovery date (NAICS 711 receipts above 2008 in 2011, profits in 2010) is row 11's evidence; extends merged Q1c-006.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2) and CANON B4: a dated fact for 2008-09 only, receipts back above 2008 in 2011, a year before shares regained end-2007 (index 1.086 checks); say same downturn, not always the same months, never a lag rule (SKELETON 2.3, Q1-044); supports a downturn reaching the deposit as delay (Q12-001).
Wed 18 Nov: store: employer jobs in 711510, -7.2% in 2009, back above 2007 only in 2013 (checks); companies with staff, not a self-employed writer (row 15).
Wed 18 Nov: store: the employer wage bill's 2009 dip (-4.71%) came from fewer jobs, pay per job +2.7% (checks); employer side only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2), CANON B4 against side: checks (five down years with shares +17.8% to +32.2%; correlations -0.18 and +0.26), but it is companies with staff (average pay $162,014), not a writer (row 15); drop the career follows a year later and two losses back to back (lag rule, SKELETON 2.3; Q1b-001); say same downturn, not always the same months, never as if l.9 or the pitch were wrong.
Wed 18 Nov: method note for whoever cites: census and tax series speak for a self-employed writer, QCEW for companies with staff (about 18 to 1; checks).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2), 2020 against l.9's same period: quote the IRS's largest percentage decrease only with the sector named (arts, entertainment and recreation, with gyms and amusement parks shut by lockdown); for a writer lead with Q1c-010's Census -12.4%; 11 times checks.
Wed 18 Nov: store data only: NAICS 711 levels for 2020-21; without 2019 the 2020 fall cannot be computed, so no part can use it yet.
Wed 18 Nov: store: after 2020 tax-data profits were back in a year and receipts in two (checks); arts sector with gyms; TY2022 from an excerpt.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: the 2020 employer drop fell in one quarter and on lower-paid staff; the monthly figures are not in the data file; no part.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 18 (back within one to two years after 2020); employer side; 2022 jobs derived.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2): 2009 made each business's receipts smaller, 2020 cut the count (checks: -0.8% and -5.4%; -9.9% and -2.8%); say businesses counted, never artists filed, and drop stops the work, since businesses under $1,000 leave the count.
Wed 18 Nov: same BEA point as Q1b-022 and Q1c-009 (2020 against shares; vintages differ); the gross output figures check and travel with it; never join vintages.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q1c-008's guard (BEA rises in 2009, so cite tax and census, never the national accounts); Q1b-023 is the whole arts economy.
Wed 18 Nov: Q1b-022's 2022 point (shares fell, the occupation rose) with QCEW and IRS added; checks; partly catch-up from 2020.
Wed 18 Nov: 2023 and 2025 are two of row 14's five down years with shares up (checks); BEA 2023 is Q1c-009's.

Wed 18 Nov: store method note: BEA's artists' account is ending, so cite IRS and Census; never a Table 3 watch: these series appear two to three years late (the newest IRS bulletin read is tax year 2022, published 2025), so none can warn before January 2028; Table 3 row 1 watches the deposit itself (Q12-001).

Wed 18 Nov: residency store: Taiwan publishing -7.2% in 2009 (checks), but the quote says 2009 had not yet recovered from the 2008 shock (Q50-037: 2008 hit hard) and 2007-08 was not read, so never dates its slump to 2009 or later for Taiwan; firms' revenue, never government arts money.
Wed 18 Nov: residency store: wider scope, publishing -5.7% then +10.2%, books -1.2% then +17.3% (checks); levels clash with row 27, so quote one report and name it.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: Taiwan publishing firms -2.0% in 2009, not back by 2012 (checks); no part.

Wed 18 Nov: residency store and a correction: Taiwan comics slid 2016-22 (-25.5%, checks; the 2021 and 2024 reports' vintages joined), and Q56-027's -31% is books, not comics (checks), in line with never her genre fell by a third.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: Taiwan print comics context for the residency's audience; never for Laura's income.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: drop the kind of thing a residency runs: comic houses are paid reading rooms, and the residency's running costs are the ten owned payments, which no closure touches.
Wed 18 Nov: store method note: name the measure whenever Taiwan's book market is quoted (tax-based +6.25% against survey -5.47% in 2021; checks).

Wed 18 Nov: the sizes agree (-5.7% to -7.2% against -6.2% to -7.8%), but Taiwan's 2007-08 change was not read and the 2010 report speaks of the 2008 shock, so drop not 2008 for Taiwan; publishers' revenue is not authors' receipts.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2) and CANON B4's evidence, matching its PARTLY: holds for 2008-09 as one episode on census, tax and employer data, fails for 2020; fix before use: not BEA's national accounts (row 23), not Taiwan's later (2007-08 unread), and name the 2020 measure (Census receipts -12.4%, IRS arts receipts -23.4%, the employer wage bill only -8.8%; 26% is profits).

Wed 18 Nov: its usable clause (her income touches the plan only through the 2028 deposit) is Q134-039's; the rest is a lag reading SKELETON 2.3 bans, and Laura draws nothing from the portfolio, so the two losses add up describes another writer, not her.
Wed 18 Nov: guard for every sentence using rows 1-25: say artists, writers and performers, never authors; the IRS stops at NAICS 711 and no US series isolates authors.
